title: Checks for return {value} statements in functions that also contain yield or yield from statements.
summary: Using return {value} in a generator function was syntactically invalid in Python 2. In Python 3 return {value} _can_ be used in a generator; however, the combination of yield and return can lead to confusing behavior, as the return statement will cause the generator to raise StopIteration with the value provided, rather than returning the value to the caller. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear. It is in preview.
message_templates: Using `yield` and `return {}` in a generator function can lead to confusing behavior

title: Checks for classes that only have a public __init__ method, without base classes and decorators.
summary: Classes with just an __init__ are possibly better off being a dataclass or a namedtuple, which have less boilerplate. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear. It is in preview.
message_templates: Class could be dataclass or namedtuple

title: Checks for raise statements in exception handlers that lack a from clause.
summary: In Python, raise can be used with or without an exception from which the current exception is derived. This is known as exception chaining. When printing the stack trace, chained exceptions are displayed in such a way so as make it easier to trace the exception back to its root cause. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.138.
message_templates: Within an `except*` clause, raise exceptions with `raise ... from err` or `raise ... from None` to distinguish them from errors in exception handling
Within an `except` clause, raise exceptions with `raise ... from err` or `raise ... from None` to distinguish them from errors in exception handling

title: Checks for zip calls without an explicit strict parameter when called with two or more iterables, or any starred argument.
summary: By default, if the iterables passed to zip are of different lengths, the resulting iterator will be silently truncated to the length of the shortest iterable. This can lead to subtle bugs. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.167.

title: Checks for mutations to an iterable during a loop iteration.
summary: When iterating over an iterable, mutating the iterable can lead to unexpected behavior, like skipping elements or infinite loops. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear. It is in preview.
message_templates: Mutation to loop iterable `{}` during iteration
Mutation to loop iterable during iteration

title: Checks for itertools.batched calls without an explicit strict parameter.
summary: By default, if the length of the iterable is not divisible by the second argument to itertools.batched, the last batch will be shorter than the rest. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in 0.10.0.

title: Checks for map calls without an explicit strict parameter when called with two or more iterables, or any starred argument.
summary: By default, if the iterables passed to map are of different lengths, the resulting iterator will be silently truncated to the length of the shortest iterable. This can lead to subtle bugs. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in 0.15.0.
